title: Egress Sharding and GPU Tenant Bandwidth Fencing Patterns
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview
--------
This document describes a repeatable pattern we use at Redwood for isolating and policing network egress from GPU tenant workloads across multi-account and multi-VPC deployments. The goal is to provide predictable bandwidth behavior, clear cost accountability, and automated failover while minimizing per-tenant networking complexity. This pattern is intended for Dedicated and Private customers and internal tenant-like isolation for self-serve usage tiers.

Goals
-----
- Enforce per-tenant egress budgets and soft/hard bandwidth caps.
- Provide predictable tail latency for real-time inference by preventing noisy-neighbor egress spikes.
- Make egress policing observable and billable per customer.
- Integrate with Terraform IaC, CI/CD pipelines, and infra runbooks for safe rollout and rollback.

When to use this pattern
------------------------
Use egress sharding and bandwidth fencing when all of the following are true:
1) Tenants generate >100 GB/day egress or are charged for egress.
2) Tenant egress behaviors affect inference latency for co-located workloads.
3) Compliance requires clear network-residency boundaries between tenants.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
- Per-tenant egress gateway: a lightweight L4 proxy + egress NAT that tags flows with tenant IDs. Implemented as an autoscaled deployment in the tenant VPC (or shared egress VPC for hoster-managed).
- Traffic sharder: sessions are routed across multiple egress gateways using a deterministic hash (tenant_id % N) to keep bandwidth segmentation stable during autoscaling.
- Bandwidth fence: token-bucket policers applied at the edge (gateway ENI) and the transit router (transit gateway/private NLB) enforced using cloud QoS features or in-host tc/iptables where cloud limits cannot shape.
- Telemetry sink: VPC flow logs + gateway metrics + per-tenant eBPF counters aggregated to the observability stack (Prometheus -> ClickHouse) for billing and alerting.

Key components and responsibilities
-----------------------------------
- module/network-egress-gateway (Terraform): creates the ASG/EKS service, IAM, ENIs, and route attachments.
- module/egress-policer (Terraform): configures cloud-level bandwidth policies (where available) and bootstrap user-data scripts to apply iproute2/tc shaping on the gateway instances.
- Observability: ingress/egress volumetrics, 95th/99th percentile per-tenant egress rate, and per-flow latency exposed on dashboards.
- Billing pipeline: daily export of per-tenant egress bytes to the billing service with tags for model, route, and priority class.

Operational SLOs and thresholds
-------------------------------
- SLO: 99.9% of inference requests experience no >10ms tail increase due to tenant egress contention.
- Alert (P1): Any tenant exceeds their hard egress cap continuously for 15 minutes. Trigger: per-tenant egress_rate > hard_cap for 15m.
- Alert (P2): Aggregate GPU-host egress utilization > 85% for 5 minutes.

Capacity and sizing guidance
---------------------------
- Gateway sizing table (baseline):
| tenant_class | expected_peak_mb_s | gateway_count_per_tenant | recommended_instance |
| small        | 50                 | 1                        | t3.small-equivalent   |
| medium       | 200                | 2                        | c6i.large-equivalent  |
| large        | 800                | 4                        | c6i.xlarge-equivalent |

- Hash shard count: We recommend N = power_of_two(>= number_of_gateways_total / 10). Keep N stable across rollouts to avoid rerouting storms.

Terraform usage example
-----------------------
- Example module invocation (HCL):

module "tenant_egress_gateway" {
  source            = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/modules.git//network-egress-gateway?ref=v1.4.0"
  tenant_id         = var.tenant_id
  vpc_id            = var.tenant_vpc_id
  subnets           = var.tenant_public_subnets
  instance_type     = var.egress_instance_type
  desired_capacity  = var.egress_desired_capacity
  bandwidth_soft_kbps = var.bandwidth_soft_kbps # token-bucket soft limit
  bandwidth_hard_kbps = var.bandwidth_hard_kbps # immediate drop if exceeded
  tags = {
    Name = "egress-gw-${var.tenant_id}"
    Owner = "platform-networking"
  }
}

- CI/CD considerations:
  - Module changes that affect iptables/user-data or kernel flags must be gated by an integration test that runs a synthetic egress storm and validates isolation on a staging cluster.
  - Use feature flags in the module to flip enforcement mode between "monitoring-only" and "enforced" to allow gradual rollout.

Runbook: Tenant hard-cap violation (oncall play)
------------------------------------------------
1) Pager triggers with alert: "tenant X hard egress cap exceeded for 15m".
2) Oncall pulls the tenant dashboard and verifies flows: check gateway pods, per-tenant eBPF counters, and VPC flow logs.
3) If traffic is legitimate (customer report):
   - Notify account owner and customer success.
   - If immediate relief required, scale up the tenant egress gateway (terraform apply var.desired_capacity++) or temporarily raise hard_cap via remote config.
4) If traffic is suspect (abuse/spike):
   - Flip enforcement to hard-drop on offending CIDR using the gateway admin endpoint.
   - Collect pcap of offending flows (gateway admin -> /capture) and upload to /secure-storage/egress-incidents/<tenant>/<date>.
5) Post-incident: open a ticket with tenant owner, attach timeline, root cause, and recommended remediation (throttling, pricing changes, or address whitelisting).

Testing and rollout plan
------------------------
- Canary strategy: deploy the module in "monitoring-only" mode to 5% of tenants for 1 week, review false-positive rates, then enable "enforced" mode for the next 10% group.
- Preflight checks (automated):
  - Terraform plan must not modify existing route tables other than new attachments.
  - e2e test: synthetic inference clients run at expected p95 QPS for 30m and verify per-tenant egress isolation metrics.

Observability and billing schema
-------------------------------
- Minimal metric set per tenant:
  - tenant.egress.bytes (counter)
  - tenant.egress.kbps (gauge, 10s rollup)
  - tenant.egress.hard_cap_violations (counter)
  - gateway.cpu/utilization, gateway.net.tx_kbps, gateway.net.rx_kbps

- Billing export CSV columns:
  Date, tenant_id, egress_bytes, route, model_tag, priority_class, cost_allocated_usd

Security and networking constraints
----------------------------------
- Gateways must run in private subnets with egress NAT to prevent public IP exposure of inference workloads.
- Internal TLS termination is required for control APIs; data plane may use mTLS where supported.
- IAM: a dedicated role egress-gateway-role with least privilege for S3 uploads (billing) and CloudWatch metrics publishing.

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands
-----------------------------------------
- Show tc qdisc and token bucket on gateway instance:
  sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0

- Dump per-tenant eBPF counters (example):
  sudo bpftool cgroup list -j | jq .
  sudo bpftool map lookup name tenant_counters key hex 0x<tenant-id>

- Quick diagnostic to replay VPC flow logs (last 1 hour):
  aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /vpc/flowlogs --filter-pattern "tenant=${TENANT_ID}" --start-time $(date -d '-1 hour' +%s)000

Ownership and next steps
------------------------
- Primary owner: platform-networking (Slack: #infra-networking).
- Secondary owner: gpu-capacity (for sizing adjustments during model rollouts).
- Next work items:
  1) Add ingress-level shaping in the model-serving runtime for ultra-low-latency customers.
  2) Replace user-data shaping with eBPF-based policers to reduce jitter.

References
----------
- Internal: module/network-egress-gateway README, module/egress-policer README.
- External: RFC for token-bucket policing and TC documentation (man tc).
